$comment: What the shipped app actually exposes, checked against the Inscribe product source. protocol-coverage.json records which creation operations the Core protocol registry says Inscribe implements. This file records three further facts the registry does not carry: whether the protocol has a workspace of its own, what the product's own production contract classifies it as, and whether a deployment must switch it on. scripts/check-capability-truth.mjs fails the build if the two files disagree.

productionStates.core: Released, ungated, and covered by the release health and smoke contract. If one of these is broken, the release is broken.
productionStates.enabled: Released and intended for production. A deployment still decides whether to switch it on, so a given build may have it off.
productionStates.incomplete: Not released. The work exists in the codebase and is not finished. Treat it as unavailable, whatever a build flag says.
productionStates.not-implemented: Inscribe has no creation workspace for this protocol at all. It appears only in read-only surfaces.

gatingNote: A gated workspace stays visible and reachable by its URL when its deployment flag is off. What stops is reading, writing, payment and order recovery, so a page can be open and still refuse to act. Two surfaces are the exception and return the 404 page instead: Recover Sats, and the Dogecoin BlockPad.

atomicals.note: The production contract records the Atomicals family through its NFT and Realms entries rather than a general Atomicals one.

subrealms.note: Subrealms have no workspace of their own. They are claimed and paid for inside the Realms workspace, which is where the production contract records those operations.

doginals.note: Doginals have no workspace of their own. Their orders run through the Dogecoin feature that also serves TAP on Doge.

cat20.note: Not released. The workspace is reachable and its transaction features stay fail-closed while the required Fractal data and signing dependencies are unavailable.

avm.note: Not released. The contract editor and academy are reachable, but deploying a contract is not a released operation.

bitmap.note: No creation workspace. Bitmap appears in Inscribe only in read-only surfaces: portfolio classification, inscription search, and the asset inventory for an output.

unat.note: No creation workspace. UNAT appears in Inscribe only in read-only surfaces: portfolio classification, inscription search, and the asset inventory for an output.

drc20.note: No creation workspace. DRC-20 appears in Inscribe only in read-only surfaces: portfolio classification and the asset inventory for an output.
